Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Russia Strikes Kherson Region, Injures 22 Civilians — Russian forces injured 22 civilians in the Kherson region on Thursday, Aug. 6, using artillery and multiple types of drones. According to the regional authorities, first-person-view (FPV) drones struck buses carrying passengers twice, while additional drone attacks wounded other civilians and damaged homes, hospitals and private vehicles.

Ex-Defense Minister Fedorov Says Ukraine Must Strike Russian Missile Launchers, Addresses Possible Return — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said Thursday, Aug. 6, that Ukraine’s best defense against Russian ballistic missiles is striking their launch crews directly, citing a successful test of a long-delayed domestic missile program amid critical shortages of Patriot interceptors. He also addressed his political future, saying he has “no moral right” to pursue other work other than work

Azerbaijan's FM Bayramov Makes First Wartime Visit to Ukraine — Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov visited Ukraine for the first time since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, touring Irpin and meeting President Volodymyr Zelensky. The trip follows a mid-July meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, where both sides reaffirmed an April cooperation plan.

Zelensky Orders ‘Special Sanctions Operation’ Plan Targeting Russia's Military Industry — President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered authorities to draft a targeted sanctions operation against Russia’s military industry, warning that foreign-made components remain critical to Russian weapons. Preventing Moscow from adapting to restrictions remains the top priority, according to the president.

Russia Doubles Military Training for Children Through 2036, Including in Occupied Parts of Ukraine — Russia is expanding military training for children, including in occupied Ukrainian territories, and raising the share of mandatory instruction to 50% of school time from Sept. 1, 2026. Human right groups warned Wednesday, Aug. 5 that the program, planned through 2036, targets both boys and girls to build a future mobilization reserve.

Ukraine Burns While Trump Fiddles — Trump's reversal on licensing Ukraine to produce Patriot interceptors – paired with US munitions stocks depleted by the Iran conflict – has signaled weakness to Putin at a critical moment. With Russian ballistic strikes intensifying ahead of winter and Duma elections looming, both sides are racing to shift the war's momentum: Ukraine through deep strikes on Russian refineries and Black Sea attacks, Russia through infrastructure destruction. Trump's incoherence

Ukraine’s New Commander Names Combat-Tested General to Number Two Job — Ukraine promotes Gen. Serhii Sobko, a battle-tested, NATO-trained reform advocate, as AFU vice commander. The 42-year-old Hero of Ukraine medal winner helped defend Kyiv in 2022 and is a “new generation” fighting officer critical of Soviet traditions.

Ex-Deputy PM Stefanishyna Charged in Graft Case — Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office charged former Deputy Prime Minister Olha Stefanishyna with illicit enrichment involving more than Hr.13.9 million ($334,000) and filing false asset declarations. Investigators allege she concealed several high-value assets and obtained property beyond her declared income.

Lithuania Discovers Underground Tunnel Dug From Belarus to Smuggle Migrants — Lithuanian border guards have discovered an unfinished underground tunnel dug from Belarus beneath the countries’ border fence, allegedly intended to smuggle migrants into Lithuania. The passage, found near Druskininkai, is the third tunnel uncovered by authorities in recent weeks amid growing border security concerns.

Ukraine’s Fire Point Builds ‘Patriot Alternative’ With Europe, Eyes 2027 Missile Interception — Fire Point has secured agreements with 13 European defense companies to supply key technologies for its Freyja missile defense system. The company aims to conduct its first successful ballistic missile interception by mid-2027 while developing a lower-cost alternative to the Patriot system.

Are Russia Sanctions in US Senate Going Sideways? — A bipartisan push to fast-track a Senate bill imposing tougher sanctions on Russia faces delays after one Democratic senator placed a hold on the legislation. Supporters warn the delay could weaken rare congressional unity and slow efforts to pressure Moscow while Ukraine continues its fight.

Trump’s Top Peace Envoys Set for First Kyiv Trip as Ukraine Seeks War Exit Talks — Acting Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha confirmed that US President Donald Trump's envoys plan to visit Ukraine to revive peace negotiations. He said Kyiv welcomes greater US engagement, arguing that a just peace and credible security guarantees cannot be achieved without Washington.

Russia’s Disinformation War Targets Germany’s Local Elections — Russia is expanding disinformation efforts ahead of Germany’s September local elections, targeting candidates with fake media content and accusations while amplifying political divisions. German officials say Kremlin-linked groups, including the Social Design Agency, aim to weaken trust in institutions and destabilize NATO countries through coordinated influence operations.

Wildberries Warehouse Damaged in Latest Ukrainian Drone Strike as Russia Reports 600+ UAVs Downed — Russian authorities said debris from a Ukrainian drone damaged a Wildberries logistics warehouse in Russia's Tver region, with no casualties reported. The claims came after Moscow said it intercepted 605 drones overnight, while regional reports also described a fire near a refinery in Yaroslavl.

‘Putin’s Defeat in Ukraine Necessary for a Free Belarus,’ Exiled Opposition Leader Says — Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said Ukraine’s victory over Russia is essential for Belarus’s freedom, warning that a Kremlin win would cement Moscow’s control over her country. She urged Western leaders to include Belarus in any negotiations on ending Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Zaluzhny: Russia Has Found Counters to Nearly Every NATO Weapon, Alliance Must Reinvent Itself — Former Commander-in-Chief Valerii Zaluzhny said Russia has developed countermeasures to nearly every major NATO weapon used in Ukraine, arguing the alliance must overhaul its military doctrine. He said Ukraine’s battlefield experience has outpaced NATO standards and that only a transformed alliance would be ready for Ukraine’s membership.

Russian Strike Hits Wheat Ship in Black Sea, 1 Killed — A Russian strike hit a Guinea-Bissau-flagged dry cargo vessel carrying Ukrainian wheat in the Black Sea, killing one person and injuring three others. The attack damaged the ship’s hull and sparked a fire, highlighting continued threats to civilian shipping and global food security.

Trump Dismisses Reports of Munitions Shortages, Says US Has ‘Massive Amount’ — President Donald Trump dismissed reports of US weapons shortages amid the Iran war, claiming America has “massive amounts” of munitions and threatening legal action against alleged leakers. Reports said depleted missile stocks had affected US military planning.

Ukraine Has Restored Full US Intelligence Support Since 2025 Freeze, Boosting Strikes Inside Russia — The United States has restored full intelligence sharing with Ukraine after a temporary freeze in 2025, helping Kyiv carry out more effective long-range strikes inside Russia, Politico reported. US lawmakers and experts say renewed cooperation has strengthened Ukraine’s battlefield position and increased pressure on Moscow.

Impact of Ukrainian Drone Attacks in Russia? — Russian missiles are raining down on Kyiv while Ukraine is striking targets in Russia and on the Russian-occupied Crimean Peninsula. In recent days, refineries and logistics centres belonging to online retailer Wildberries have again come under attack and been set on fire by Ukrainian drones.

Ukraine Hits Russia’s Top-5 Oil Refinery as Fuel Shortages Spread Across Country — Ukrainian drones struck one of Russia’s largest oil refineries for the seventh time this year, sparking a fire at the Slavneft-YANOS facility in Yaroslavl. The attack comes as Kyiv’s strikes on Russian energy infrastructure deepen Moscow’s fuel shortages and disrupt oil refining capacity.
Russia Denies Using Colombian Mercenaries in Ukraine War — Russia’s embassy in Colombia denied links to alleged networks recruiting Colombian fighters for Moscow’s war against Ukraine.

US Senator Links Kyiv Deaths to Delays on Russia Sanctions and Air Defense Aid — Sen. Jeanne Shaheen linked the latest Russian strike near Kyiv to delays in tougher sanctions and air defense support, urging Congress to act after 17 people were killed. The Senate has already voted 86–12 to advance a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Russia’s energy and financial sectors.

Zelensky Urges Interceptor Release After All 28 Missiles Go Unintercepted, Killing 17 in Kyiv Region — President Volodymyr Zelensky urged allies to speed up deliveries of air defense interceptors after a Russian missile and drone barrage killed 17 people in the Kyiv region. He said Ukraine and NATO chief Mark Rutte coordinated efforts with countries that have the missiles and capacity to help.

Germany Warns of ‘New Level of Danger’ After Explosives-Laden Drone Found Near Ukrainian Plane — German police found an explosives-laden drone near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane at Leipzig-Halle Airport, forcing flight diversions and a bomb-disposal operation. A second cargo aircraft also collided with an unidentified flying object nearby and landed safely with minor damage.

Russian Geran-2 Drone Wreckage Found in Moldova — Fragments of a Russian Geran-2 attack drone were discovered in southern Moldova near the Ukrainian border. Authorities launched a forensic investigation into how the drone had entered Moldovan territory.

This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. Koretskyi Orders Warehouse Dispersal Plan Following Russian Strikes on Supply Chains — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi ordered authorities to identify backup warehouse space within three days, while pledging new credit support mechanisms to address disruptions caused by Russian strikes on supply enterprises.

Head of Ukrainian Search Unit Yukov Killed While Exhuming Bodies — Oleksii Yukov, the 40-year-old head of Ukraine’s search unit Platsdarm, was killed on Wednesday, Aug. 5, while exhuming bodies in the Donetsk region. He had spent more than two decades recovering fallen soldiers’ remains.

Russian State Hackers Target Hotel Wi-fi to Spy on Travelers, Microsoft Reports — A Russian intelligence-linked hacking group has been hijacking hotel and conference center Wi-Fi networks to steal corporate travelers’ login credentials, Microsoft says. The group reportedly uses AI tools to power the operation, dubbed CaptiveCrunch.

Russia Is Losing the War. The Numbers Prove It — Pundits call it a “Russia’s advance.”
The numbers call it systemic collapse: 39,500 casualties for 30 km² of rubble.
The real balance sheet:

Russian Strike on Dnipropetrovsk Region Injures 1, Cuts Power for 55,000 — Russian forces struck five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 50 times on Wednesday, Aug. 5, injuring one person, while damaging civilian infrastructure, including private homes and a school. More than 55,000 residents lost power in the Nikopol area alone.

UK Defense Chief Streeting Visits Kyiv for First Time — President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv on Wednesday, Aug. 5, where the two discussed missile defense and joint arms production. The visit followed a Russian strike that killed at least 17 people.

Zelensky 40-Day Plan to Force Russian Talks With Drones – Huge Damage, But No Peace — Ukraine’s 40-day drone campaign failed to force a ceasefire but damaged Russian logistics, hitting bases, warehouses, ships and supply routes. Hundreds of drones targeted Crimea links and fuel networks, causing disruption, shortages and costly damage.

Putin Replaces Key Ukraine Commanders as Russia’s Donbas Offensive Slows — Vladimir Putin replaced commanders overseeing two key military groupings in Ukraine. The reshuffle comes as Russia’s advance slows and analysts question whether Moscow can capture the remainder of the Donetsk region even in 2027.

Russia Strikes Epicentr, Nova Poshta, Silpo, Novus Warehouses, Killing at Least 10 — Russian missiles and drones hit logistics facilities belonging to Epicentr, Nova Poshta, Silpo, and Novus overnight on Wednesday, killing at least 10 people. A night earlier, drones destroyed a Biosphere Corporation warehouse in Dnipro.

Moscow Blast Kills Russian Air Force Chief’s Son-in-Law — Russian state records confirm that Danylo Peredriy, the son-in-law of Russian Aerospace Forces commander Aleksandr Chayko, died following the Aug. 1 bombing at Moscow’s Balzi Rossi restaurant. Reports also suggest Chayko’s daughter was injured, while pro-war Russian bloggers claim the commander himself may have been the intended target.

Russia May Launch 100 Ballistic Missiles at Ukraine Every Month — Russia could continue launching about 100 ballistic missiles a month while increasingly targeting Ukrainian businesses and logistics infrastructure, presidential adviser Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov said.

Ex-European Officials Met Unnamed Kremlin Veteran for Secret Ukraine Talks — Former senior European officials held private discussions with an unidentified former Kremlin official in Vienna in July, Bloomberg reported. The participants acted independently rather than on behalf of their governments, and no Ukrainian representative was identified in the report.

Zelensky Addresses Ambassadors: Weapons Needed in Ukraine, Not Warehouses — President Volodymyr Zelensky delivered a major address to Ukrainian ambassadors gathered in Kyiv, stating that, ahead of what is expected to be a difficult winter, the diplomatic corps must refocus its mission to get host nations to provide Ukraine with weapons.

Russian FPV Drone Developer Critically Injured in Car Bombing Near Yekaterinburg — Vladimir Tkachuk, general director of Uraldronzavod and developer of the Upyr FPV attack drone used by Russian forces in Ukraine, was critically injured in a car bombing near Yekaterinburg on Wednesday, according to Russian media reports. Investigators have opened a criminal case for attempted murder.

Former Ukraine Envoy to US Stefanishyna Receives New Corruption Notice of Suspicion — Former Deputy Prime Minister and ex-ambassador to the US Olha Stefanishyna has received a new corruption notice of suspicion from Ukraine’s anti-graft agencies, with a court now considering a preventive measure against her.

Ukraine’s Air Defense Missile Supplies Drop Threefold as Kyiv Warns Partners Have Stockpiles Available — Ukraine’s air defense missile supplies have dropped threefold compared with 2025, Zelensky said, warning that Kyiv faces growing shortages as Russia intensifies ballistic missile attacks. The shortfall comes amid reports that Washington rejected Ukraine’s request for additional Patriot interceptors and scaled back earlier commitments.

The 40-Day Operation Deadline — On Aug. 4 the 40-day operation announced by Zelensky to pressure Russia into a ceasefire came to an end. While few were expecting Russia to stop, the announcement also had other aims meant to ratchet up pressure.

Drone With Detonator Found Near Ukrainian Plane at Leipzig Airport — German authorities found a drone carrying a package with a detonator near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport shortly before midnight on Tuesday, Aug. 5, Bild reported. Investigators classified the device as a potential explosive. The airport was shut down for nearly two hours while bomb disposal teams responded. A cargo plane that had to abort landing later collided with an unknown object about 6 km from t

EU Chief Slams Russian ‘Atrocities’ After Kyiv Attack — EU chief Ursula von der Leyen condemned Russia’s latest deadly attack on Kyiv and said Ukraine will receive another €1.4 billion in profits generated from frozen Russian assets. The funds are part of a broader EU effort to make Moscow pay for its war and support Ukraine’s defense.

Russia Is Back to Banning Books — As Vladimir Putin continues to limit the amount and type of information allowed to circulate through his realm, the Soviet penchant for banning books and punishing those in their possession is experiencing a revival. The US needs to combat this trends as it did during the Cold War.

Czechia Ends Temporary Protection for Draft-Age Ukrainian Men — The Czech Interior Ministry said new EU rules will deny temporary protection to newly arriving Ukrainian men of military age who cannot prove they have met their military obligations. The decision also extends temporary protection for eligible Ukrainians until March 2028.

What Zelensky’s 40-Day Oil Campaign Achieved – and What It Didn’t — Even though Russia has not been brought anywhere near to a ceasefire, Ukraine’s 40-day campaign has achieved one major goal. Russia’s strategic depth – the assumption that its refineries, its budget, and its own annexed peninsula sat safely behind the front line – no longer holds.

They Missed the Last Train: Russian Strike Kills 8 at Kyiv Region Station — Eight people were killed at Kvitneve railway station in Kyiv region after missing their last train, a local official said. The station was struck during a Russian missile-and-drone barrage that killed at least 17 people across Kyiv and the surrounding region.

North Korea May Deploy Missile Unit to Russia for Strikes on Ukraine, Kyiv Intel Warns — North Korea is preparing to deploy a missile unit to western Russia that could operate up to 120 ballistic missiles for strikes on Ukraine, a Ukrainian military intelligence official told Reuters. The move would mark another major escalation in military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang.

Ukraine Strikes Wildberries Warehouse in Russia, Putting 8th Major Logistics Hub Out of Action — A Ukrainian drone attack damaged a major Wildberries logistics center in Russia's Tula region, forcing it to suspend operations. According to independent Russian outlet Agentstvo, eight of the marketplace's 15 largest warehouses have now stopped operating following Ukrainian strikes.

NATO Membership Now Irrelevant for Ukraine? — Former Ukrainian military chief Valeriy Zaluzhnyi’s claim that NATO membership is no longer central to Ukraine’s security debate raises a deeper question: did Russia’s invasion achieve the opposite of its stated goals? Timothy Ash argues that Moscow’s war has strengthened Ukraine’s military and pushed Europe toward a historic defense buildup.

Russian Strike Triggers Ammonia Leak in Kyiv; Emergency Crews Contain Threat — A Russian missile strike damaged a specialized ammonia tank in Kyiv’s Holosiivskyi district, causing a leak during a wider overnight assault. Emergency crews contained it by 2:10 a.m., and officials said nearby residents were not at risk.

Ukraine’s Strikes Bring Blackouts, Fuel Shortages and ‘Road of Death’ to Occupied Crimea — Ukraine’s intensified strikes on occupied Crimea are disrupting fuel supplies, power infrastructure and Russian logistics. Residents face blackouts, soaring petrol prices and increasingly dangerous routes linking the peninsula to Russia.

Children’s Hospital in Zaporizhzhia Hit by Russian Strike; Children and Medics Saved by Shelter — Russian forces struck the grounds of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Children’s Clinical Hospital, damaging its facade and windows. All children and medical staff were in a shelter and survived unharmed.

Chilling Video of Kherson Vegetable Seller Stalked by Russian Drone Goes Viral — Footage from Kherson shows an FPV drone pursuing 52-year-old Yuriy around his vegetable truck before exploding. He survived, but the attack mirrors a wider pattern documented by the UN of civilians near the front being hunted during ordinary daily tasks.

17 Killed in Russia’s Third Kyiv Barrage in a Week Amid Critical Patriot Shortage — Russia launched another combined drone and ballistic missile assault on Kyiv, killing 15 people and injuring 22. Residential and non-residential buildings were damaged, an ambulance was hit, and an ammonia leak was contained.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Zelensky: Kyiv in ‘Daily Contact’ With Trump Team, Some Work Remains ‘Non-Public’ — Zelensky said Ukraine is in daily contact with Trump’s team and ready for meetings in any format. He expects Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to step up in August, while some diplomatic work with other partners remains “non-public.”

Ukraine Repels Russian Assaults Across 12 Frontline Axes on Tuesday — The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) repelled Russian assaults across multiple axes on Tuesday, Aug. 4, with the Pokrovsk axis seeing 23 attacks. Russian forces carried out 216 combat clashes, fired 6,428 kamikaze drones, and dropped 213 guided bombs (KABs), according to Ukraine's General Staff.

India Declines Russia’s Offer to Purchase Su-57E Fighter Jets — India has declined Russia’s offer to purchase Su-57E stealth fighter jets, choosing instead to modernize its roughly 260-strong Su-30MKI fleet and push forward its domestically produced Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program.

Russia Lost 30,272 Troops to Ukrainian Drone Strikes in July Alone, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian drone strikes killed or badly wounded 30,272 Russian troops in July alone, based only on cases with clear video evidence. He praised Ukraine’s Security Service’s (SSU) Alpha unit for leading in successful target engagements.

New Law Grants Equal Military Rights to Ukraine’s Former Convict Soldiers — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a new law on Tuesday Aug. 4, granting former convicts serving under military contract the same rights as other soldiers, including medical care, leave, and transfer options. Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, passed the bill on July 14 with 309 votes in favor.

Zelensky Sets 3 Priorities to Speed up Ukraine’s EU Accession Bid — President Volodymyr Zelensky outlined three main priorities for accelerating Ukraine’s EU accession bid on Tuesday, Aug. 4, framing EU membership as a security matter instead of just an economic one. Two negotiation clusters have opened since mid-June, with four more in preparation.

Syria To Cut Russian Oil Imports per US Request — According to Reuters’ sources, Syria has told the US it is willing to drastically cut Russian oil imports as part of talks on removing its remaining terrorism sanctions designation. The pledge comes as Damascus seeks to diversify its energy supply.

Ozon Stops Calling Crimea Part of Russia in Support Chat — A TikTok video circulating online claims Russian e-commerce platform Ozon no longer treats occupied Crimea as part of Russia in customer support responses. Kyiv Post could not independently verify whether the response reflects an official policy or an isolated support message.

Ukraine's Economy Grows 0.6% in Q2 2026, Trails NBU's Estimate — Ukraine's economy grew 0.6% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, a flash estimate from the State Statistics Service showed, falling short of the National Bank's 0.8% calculation. The NBU said expanded budget stimulus and an improving energy grid drove the rebound, but intensified Russian strikes on ports and business infrastructure limited faster growth.

From Licensing to the First Ukrainian-Made Patriot Missile: The Road Ukraine Must Travel — As Ukraine seeks to reduce its dependence on foreign missile supplies, the prospect of licensed Patriot interceptor production has emerged as one of the country’s most ambitious defense-industrial projects. Yet obtaining a license is only the first step in a complex journey that requires advanced technology transfer, industrial infrastructure, highly skilled personnel, and long-term strategic commitment.

One Week On: Was Zelensky’s Washington Visit Really a Success? — Zelensky appears to have repaired relations with Trump and secured a strong bipartisan display in the Senate. But Washington announced no new weapons package, the sanctions bill remains unfinished, and the proposed Patriot-production agreement is still under negotiation.

Russian Airstrikes on Kramatorsk Injure 22 Civilians — At least 22 people were injured after Russia struck central Kramatorsk with two guided aerial bombs on Tuesday. The attack hit a residential apartment building, prompting an ongoing search-and-rescue operation, according to regional authorities.

New Defense Minister Hires Ukraine’s Top Audit Firm for Due Diligence on Army Contractors — Ukraine’s new defense minister, Yevhen Khmara, is using YouControl’s digital vetting tools to fight military procurement corruption. The move targets risky contractors after scandals involving the alleged $40 million in ammunition fraud and $17 million in food overpricing.

Zelensky Greenlights New SBU Operations Against Russia — President Zelensky authorized new SBU operations against Russian aggression and approved steps to remove personnel who “work for themselves, not for Ukraine.” The announcement follows a 40-day operation approved in late June.

Georgia's Only Oil Refinery to Stop Processing Russian Crude — Black Sea Petroleum LLC, owner of Georgia's only oil refinery, confirmed on Monday, Aug. 4, that it is phasing out Russian crude oil. The Kulevi refinery began processing Kazakh-origin crude in early July and expects a shipment of Libyan crude between Aug. 20-30 under an agreement running through 2027. The move follows EU sanctions that gave the refinery until January 2027 to end Russian oil processing.

Video Shows Russian FPV Drone Chasing Civilian Through Kherson Before Exploding — A Russian FPV drone was filmed chasing a civilian through a Kherson street before exploding nearby, leaving the man injured. Ukrainian officials condemned the attack as a deliberate hunt for civilians and called it another Russian war crime requiring an international response.

SBU Says Russia Using 'Honey Traps' to Assassinate Ukrainian Soldiers — On Tuesday, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) warned that Russian intelligence services have significantly intensified efforts to assassinate Ukrainian soldiers using “honey traps” – fake online dating encounters. The SBU said it has foiled more than 50 such attempts since the start of 2026.

Ukrainian Drones Strike Syzran Oil Refinery Again, Hit More Wildberries Warehouses — Drones reportedly struck Russia’s Syzran oil refinery and a Wildberries warehouse near Tver as Moscow claimed it intercepted 320 Ukrainian UAVs overnight. The refinery had only recently resumed operations following a July attack.

Russia May Target Water Supply This Winter, Kyiv Warns — Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia’s next winter campaign may focus on Ukraine’s water infrastructure after devastating attacks on the power grid. He said Kyiv is strengthening critical infrastructure while seeking additional Patriot missiles and financial support from allies.

A Letter The Economist Conveniently Ignored — The Economist was taken to task for its shameless promotion of a man who lives and thrives at Putin’s pleasure and advocates for business as usual with Moscow. Kyiv Post presents a scathing letter to the editor that the British publication decided not to publish.

Ceuta Between a Migration Crisis and a Hybrid Attack: Giorgia Meloni’s Policy and Europe’s Security — The European Democrats’ attack on Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is politically dishonest and shows that part of Europe’s center still does not understand the world in which it lives.

2 Children Killed in Russian Guided Bomb Strike on Sumy — A Russian guided bomb attack on Sumy killed three civilians, including two girls aged 5 and 10, and damaged civilian infrastructure overnight. The strike came as Moscow continues using aerial bombs to target Ukrainian cities near the border, despite growing Ukrainian electronic warfare efforts against the weapons.

Oschadbank, Ukreximbank to Sell Gulliver Mall for $207 Million Starting Price — State-owned Oschadbank and Ukreximbank will auction Kyiv’s Gulliver multifunctional complex through the Prozorro.Sales system from September, with a $207 million floor price. The banks seized the 157,000-square-meter (1.7 million-square-foot) complex from sanctioned businessman Viktor Polishchuk’s Three O LLC in July 2025 after the borrower stopped servicing its debt.

Ukraine Strikes Wildberries Hubs Near Moscow, St. Petersburg in Fresh Drone Wave — Ukraine struck two major Wildberries logistics hubs near Moscow and St. Petersburg in overnight drone attacks, extending a campaign targeting Russia’s supply network. The latest strikes reportedly damaged one of the retailer’s largest distribution centers as Ukraine continues to pressure Russia’s logistics infrastructure deep behind the front lines.

Hysteria in Russia: ‘Nowhere to Hide’ as Putin’s Palace Falls Within Ukraine’s Reach — Drone activity near Gelendzhik has turned Putin’s $1 billion Black Sea palace into a symbol of Russia’s shrinking sense of security. As Moscow decries Ukrainian strikes, Kyiv’s growing deep-strike campaign is forcing the war back toward the state that launched it.

Kyiv Under Air Raid Alert as Russian Drones Threaten Capital, Regions — Kyiv and several Ukrainian regions were placed under air raid alert overnight amid a threat from Russian attack drones. Authorities urged residents to remain in shelters.

Umerov to Lead Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence While Retaining Chief Peace Negotiator Role — Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service while remaining Kyiv’s chief peace negotiator. His expanding portfolio also includes international Drone Deals, the Freyja anti-ballistic program and deeper intelligence cooperation with allies.

Russian Drone Strike Destroys Major Ukrainian Postal Hub, Hits Civilian Logistics Network — Russian forces struck Pryluky with three drones, destroying a Nova Poshta cargo branch and damaging warehouses with agricultural machinery. One man was wounded, while postal workers and customers sheltering at the site were unharmed.

Russia Jails Ukrainian for 24 Years in Case Rights Groups Call Politically Motivated — A Russian military court sentenced 30-year-old Ukrainian Yan Haupt to 24 years in prison over alleged plans to attack railway infrastructure in Krasnodar. Rights groups say the case is another politically motivated prosecution of a Ukrainian by Russian authorities.
